replies.author: goldenwalrus909
replies.body:
I agree, it really sucks. There should definitely be a system to prevent it like this one I mentioned in a previous comment:

The worst thing is when you're on a TDM map like Titans and there's a 5v7 with 2 donors-- there's just no way for the 5-person-team to win. I think the best way to fix this is to make a system where donors can't change the amount of players on a team by /join *team* by any more than 20%. This means if there's a match with 5v5, if you and your donator friend tried to join, both of you couldn't because you're changing the amount of players on that team using /join *team* by over 20%. If you're transferring 5 to 6, you're increasing 5 by 20%. This means when you're /join *team*ing, you're changing the player amount by 20%. Your friend then has to do play on the other team because if (s)he /join *team friend is on*, she'd increase the team amount by 40%-- you're going from 5 to 7. This can also be shown as an inequality. (If the amount of donors using /join *team* is x, and the amount of players on the other team is y,) x ≤ .2y. If there are 5 people on a team, this means only 1 can join (1 ≤ 1).
I don't exactly know which side I'm on, though, because it's fun to be with a lot of your friends but sometimes it can be unfair ):

replies.author: StaticFaultz
replies.body:
I have an idea to rule out stacking, but I don't really know if it works.

Anyways, here's my idea:
When players join a match, donators can join any team they want. However, if the team they are joining has, lets say a 10% advantage over the other team, the donator is prompted with a message saying "Blue team is overstacked. Please join the red team or wait for the red team to match the blue teams' player count by at least 10%". This could rule out major stacking, but not small 1-5% differences between the teams.

I'd say that what you are complaining about constitutes as stacking. When a two donors stack a team that has a maximum of 7 players, they're already stacking the team by 20% more than the other team that has only 7 players. But if someone complains about the kind of stacking where it's like a 40-player team and there's only 3 players more than the other team, that's sort of stupid.

replies.author: San_David
replies.body:
Here's a few ideas that some people might not have thought of...

- Give / Add Strength I (and maybe Resistance I, if neccessary) to any team with a 2 - 3 player disadvantage. Give / Add Strength (and Resist. II, maybe) to any team with a 4+ player disadvantage.

To clarfiy, here's some examples...
Team A: 7 Players
Team B: 5 Players
Team C: 4 Players
Team D: 3 Players.
So, in this situation, Team A would get no boosts, Teams B & C would get Str. (+Res.) I, and Team D would get Str. (+Res.) II.

Basically, it gives the underdogs an advantage over stacked teams, without having to force donators to another team.

-----

Another idea is to encourage bow combat. It'll allow spawncamped players to pick off enemies from their spawn, without being in great danger. And, as is, bow combat sucks in Nebula, with Archer / Sniper only getting 24 / 32 arrows, respectively, turning them almost into suicide classes.

It also adds more variety to combat as well, since Nexus is mainly about sword combat atm. And, the problem I see with sword combat is that the person with the better gear will usually win (and I say usually as in the two players have equal skill level), turning classes like Pyro and Barbarian into powerhouses. Bow combat may somewhat alleviate that.

And, to anyone that may complain about people 'camping' and 'being stupid n00bs that can't make it out of their spawn,' consider that you may be the ones keeping them in their spawn, ruining the game for them...

replies.author: San_David
replies.body:
Yes, it would be best if the effects were lost as soon as the teams are equalized, if equalized at all.

    And, with Strength II (and / or / without Resist. II) being a bit much, you have to consider that it's also a bit much for a team to be fighting at 7 v 3, or even more differential ratios, like 4 v 1. Combine that with possible spawnkilling, and it's fairly certain that you and your underwhelming team will die if you don't have buffs. Of course, they can be tweaked as well. Another possible buff (that I just thought of) is giving outmatched players more hearts / absorption health. Perhaps 2 - 4 at a two player disadvantage?

   Also, I really wouldn't call bow combat weak myself. I know that 3 - 4 bow shots, at max charge, can kill a player in full leather armor, something that a moderately skilled archer can easily do. And, if they can't, one or two shots is enough to at least weaken them a bit, allowing for an easy sword kill. That last bit is what I love about mixing sword and bow combat, it gives more viable strategies than just smacking someone with a sword, which I think Nexus lacks as a whole.

   And, to the people that complain... to put it simply, they should really just deal with it. I mean, it's rather immature of them to just confine themselves to a singular way of thinking, and not allow other styles of combat into the game. Open your minds, people!

   And...FFA. Can't wait for that, even though killstealing will be rampant. >.> Though, you might want to consider that not every map will be FFA - it just simply wouldn't work with maps like Dredmor. Maps like Candoria or Dragonblaze Peaks, however, might work wonderfully for it.
